description: MMS gate on a non-unit, non-origin domain: run the inline esm-spec 6.6 tests of problems/heat_1d_zero_grad_nonunit.esm (model HeatNonunit, test mms_neumann_decay_nonunit; heat equation on x in [-1.5, 2.5], L=4, consumer-supplied x0/dx geometry) at the problem's default resolution (N=64) through each binding's official simulation pathway. This is the executable proof that grids/cartesian_uniform_1d serves arbitrary consumer-specified extents with no library-file edits: the rule body's free dx resolves to the model's dx = 4/N observed. The assertions and their tolerances live in the problem file itself; this manifest only routes the runners.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator

python._doc: Pinned so Python temporal truncation is negligible against the spatial goldens: scipy explicit RK45 leaves ~1e-3 relative residue on the stiff heat sweep at any feasible tolerance, while LSODA at 1e-12/1e-14 agrees with the Julia Tsit5 reference to <2e-6 relative on every resolution.
